 It's not unusual for TV adaptations to stray from their source material that they become completely irrelevant to the original story. But HBO's acclaimed post-apocalyptic series never fell into that category, staying faithful to the popular video game from which it was adapted. The first season, in which Joel ( Pedro Pascal ) and his surrogate daughter Ellie (Bella Ramsey) wander through a disease-ravaged America, maps closely onto Part I of Naughty Dog's original video game. Meanwhile, Season 2, in which Joel dies, covers the first half of the game's lengthier sequel, known as Part II.

 While there was talk of The Last of Us lasting for four seasons or more, it looks as though its upcoming third season will be its last, covering the final half of the video game sequel. In line with the game, the final season, slated for a 2027 release, will tell the story from the perspective of Abby (Kaitlyn Dever), the young woman who killed Joel in Season 2 to avenge her father's death. The audience will get a glimpse of her life before she kills Joel and later confronts Ellie while holding Tommy (Gabriel Luna) at gunpoint.

 While it is unlikely that Pedro Pascal will appear in the third season of The Last of Us , Gabriel Luna praised the Chilean-born actor for his performance in a recent interview with The Hollywood Reporter . "Pedro committed such an extraordinary performance to the screen, and you know the audience is certainly holding that flame for him," the actor said. "In every action, in every life Tommy takes and in every round fired, there is that longing for his brother," he added. "I know Bella feels the same way about Ellie and the character’s grief."

 Luna also addressed the sad news that Neil Druckmann, the original creator of The Last of Us and a former co-showrunner on the show, will no longer be at the helm for its third and final season . There is reportedly no bad blood between Druckmann and showrunner Craig Mazin, who will write the remaining scripts for the show's final season. The official line is that as development ramps up, Druckmann figured it was time to leave the show to focus on his other commitments with the video game studio Naughty Dog and his next title, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet .
 Speaking about Druckmann's exit, Luna seemed to suggest it was business as usual on set. "As far as it goes for me, I have a job to do. Bella [Ramsey] and I are the longest-tenured people on this set, so we're carrying the DNA of the story, Neil's intentions and his spirit forward." He stressed that the show is in good hands with Mazin. "Craig loves the story that Neil has constructed, and he’s been a very stable steward who honors and maintains the source material... and so we carry on."

 Having never played the game, I loved the TV adaptation of TLOU....Until Joel died. Now to be honest I don't think I will bother with the last season, I couldn't give a flying fudge about Abby's story, or what happens to her. Joel did what he did to save Ellie's life. He gave her Dad the option to step away from her, then he showed him the mercy of an instant death. Abby brutally tortured and murdered Joel as revenge not for justice. So season 3 is a flop before it even hit the screen in my opinion.
